title: La Guiche (Rome 1551), Noailles (Venice 1558), Seure (Lisbon 1558): BnF fr. 3138 no. 22, fr. 3151 nos. 33, 39-44

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3138 no. 22, f. 60v (Gallica btv1b90601662 view 65)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaf, the next leaf or in the margin; the surrounding clear text gave context.

transcription.notes: First two lines struck through by the writer. The + versus barred-+ distinction may be conflated.

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3151 no. 33, f. 60r (Gallica btv1b9059865k view 61)

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment in the inner margin, partly lost in the gutter.

system.summary: La Guiche: a simple substitution of 22 invented signs for the 22-letter alphabet, no word division.
system.notes: The system covers La Guiche only; Noailles and Seure use other symbol alphabets. Seure's cipher is homophonic (~60 signs) with numeral codes.

prior_solution.where: Web search found no edition; the Noailles letter has a contemporary marginal decipherment.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded both Gallica volumes and located items 22, 33 and 39-44 from the BnF item list.
Checked for court decipherments: Noailles has one in the margin (cut by the binding); La Guiche and Seure have none.
Transcribed the La Guiche cipher (406 signs) from per-line full-resolution crops.
22 distinct signs, sign 3 at 16%: a simple substitution suspected.
Free many-to-one annealer with the fr-1530 model: collapsed onto i/x.
Permutation annealer (swap moves), 16 restarts: best run read 'le conte sainctefiore est mal satisfaict'.
Fixed F=qu, 8=p, P=y, A=v from context; refined the rest. Text reads in substance; one name and two rare signs open.
Web search for an edition of La Guiche's 1551 letters: none found.
Seure letters (nos. 39-44): ~2,000 signs, homophonic plus nomenclator, no decipherment; left open as too large for this pass.

Corrections reported while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list, checked on guiche_ct.txt, reading_raw.txt, the key and the view 65 image: L3 gives 'lamraq?adeur de senes', so the write-up's 'de ceux de Sienes' becomes 'l'am[bass]adeur de Senes' ('bass' inferred from context, grade I); 'mal satisfaict de ..., et' restores the 'de' of L5 (a four-dot sign, not transcribed, follows it); the site's portrait strip named Henry II as recipient, corrected to Montmorency (the letter closes 'Monseigneur').

Seen on the image while checking, not yet applied: a 24-sign cipher run after 'qu'il advisera' is missing from guiche_ct.txt and gives 'a la pratique qu'aves entendu' with the key; the sign transcribed t in L3 and in '+arna+e' is a plain cross distinct from the barred r, and read as b gives 'l'ambassadeur' and 'sieur Barnabe Adorne'; F c gives ss in 'ambassadeur' and 'aussi' (L12). Needs a re-transcription pass.

La Guiche f. 60v re-read on the Gallica image to fill the quotation gaps for Lasry's list: the missing 24-sign run after 'qu'il advisera' transcribed (L2x) and read 'a la pratique qu'aves entendu' with the key unchanged; the plain cross split from the barred cross as b ('l'ambassadeur', 'Barnabe Adorne' x2); ff+c = ss ('aussi'); 'du service' in L10; the four-dot sign after 'mal satisfaict de' transcribed, one occurrence, conjectured 'l'Empereur' (grade I) from the count's imperial service; clear bridge lines read so the reading runs from the Sienese envoy to Santa Fiora.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 430 tokens, 23 types, fr-1530-despatches order 4: reading -2.612 per letter; random keys -6.746 (z 6.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.679 (mean -3.704, z 31.2); annealer on the real text -2.589. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.612; polyphony 0.0; 1 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.589

outcome.method_basis: The La Guiche letter (fr. 3138 f. 60v) has no decipherment anywhere; its 22-sign substitution was broken by swap annealing with a French 5-gram model and finished by hand from context; the Noailles marginal decipherment in fr. 3151 belongs to a different letter and was not used.
outcome.notes: La Guiche read in part; Noailles read at the time; Seure open. fraction_read 0.17 is an estimate by cipher signs from the notes (La Guiche about 350 of 406, Noailles about 150 signs read at the time only in part, Seure about 2,000 signs none), not a measurement.

gaps.detail: :: occurs once (conjecture 'l'Empereur', grade I), 5 only in the struck lines; the name is read 'Barnabe Adorne' (30 Sept 2026)

outcome.fraction_read_source: Whole target not measurable: Noailles' ~150 signs are not transcribed and the Seure letters (~2,000 signs, not a document entry) are unread. La Guiche alone, counted from guiche_ct.txt (406 signs) against reading_raw.txt: ~352/406 = 0.87 read (unread: most of struck lines L0-L1, the name '+arna+e' x2 = 14 signs, 'lamraq?' in L3, three '?' signs); that line judgement is by eye. 0.17 kept as the by-sign estimate over the catalogue entry.
